newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on USDA acreage, harvest.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on USDA acreage, harvest.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on bearish USDA spring wheat acreage data, active harvesting of the hard red winter wheat crop and on a drop in soybeans, traders said.

CBOT grains and soy markets overall on Monday were rattled by a limit fall in soybean futures linked to USDA's bearish 1997 U.S. soy acreage number, while corn rose in reaction to USDA's corn acreage tally and wheat faltered.
"Another big surprise was spring wheat acres," said Dick Loewy, president of Chicago-based AgResource, Inc.
USDA Monday said U.S. farmers seeded 19.2 million acres to spring wheat this year, well above an average of analysts' expectations for 18.1 million.

Also traders said U.S. weather generally has been conducive for wheat harvesting and reports have been filtering in of excellent yields in U.S. hard red winter and soft red winter wheat growing regions.
New crop July SRW wheat set a contract low of $3.19-1/2 a bushel, below the previous low of $3.25 set Friday. The $3.19-1/2 is the lowest for a nearby contract in three years.
Overall, CBOT SRW wheat closed unchanged to four cents lower, with July down two at $3.23-3/4.
Monday's export news did little to support wheat futures, traders said.
USDA Monday said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended June 26 totalled 10.216 million bushels, well below expectations for 15 million to 17 million bushels.
Traders said wheat was underpinned by USDA's figure for wheat quarterly stocks at 444 million bushels, below an average of analysts' expectations for 466 million.
Signals the market was oversold with the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for July at 22 percent also underpinned futures, traders said. An RSI of 30 or less is considered an oversold market.
Also the posting of no deliveries Monday, first notice day for deliveries on the July, shored up the July. There had been talk that one to three million bushels of wheat may be posted for delivery.

Funds sold roughly 17.0 million bushels of wheat with Prudential Securities, Smith Barney and FIMAT Futures each selling three million bushels of September, traders said, and Term Commodities bought six million bushels of September.
In spread trading, Refco Inc did 1.5 million bushels of July/September at nine to 9-1/4 cents, premium September.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 35,000 contracts, below the 40,722 traded Friday.
In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man Interntional sold 2,000 September $3.60 puts at 30-1/2 to 31 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, sightly above the 3,903 traded Friday.
